transcript.content: Hi, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hello doctor, nice to meet you too. I'm here because my family says I’m always getting sidetracked and forgetting what I was supposed to be doing. They've gotten really worried that it might be some kind of memory problem.

Have these attention and memory problems been present since childhood, or did they start later in life after you had been functioning normally? Did they begin around the same time as a medical illness or a period of feeling depressed most days?

Actually, these issues go back to my childhood; back in primary school, my teachers always said I was daydreaming, missing instructions, and forgetting my books. It definitely didn't start with any illness or depression, but it has just become much more noticeable over the past year since I retired and started trying to juggle too many different commitments.

Along with being easily distracted, have you also had lifelong problems with restlessness or impulsive behavior, like fidgeting, interrupting people, or acting before thinking? Or has it mainly been inattention and forgetfulness?

My main struggles have always been inattention and forgetfulness, and I wouldn't say I'm impulsive, but I do experience a lot of restlessness. During long meetings or in waiting rooms, I get this inner urge to move where I'm constantly shifting in my seat and wanting to stand up. Even when trying to do quiet activities like reading, my legs get fidgety and I usually have to get up and tinker with something instead.
Have these attention problems caused clear difficulties in at least two parts of your life, such as work, home, school, or relationships? What are the main problems they have caused?

Yes, they've caused real problems both at home with my family and with my activities at the senior center because I keep double-booking myself and missing appointments. I've let small commitments fall through so much that my wife and kids have lost some trust in me and have even stopped asking me for help with certain things.

Compared with earlier in adulthood, have your attention and forgetfulness been steadily getting worse in a progressive way, or have they stayed about the same over time and mainly become more noticeable since retirement? Also, are you having other memory problems like getting lost in familiar places, repeating the same questions, or trouble managing bills or medications?

They have actually stayed about the same over my life, but they became much more noticeable this past year because retirement left me with too many unstructured commitments. I don't have any of those severe memory issues like getting lost or repeating questions, and I still feel sharp in conversation—it's really just that I get easily sidetracked and disorganized.

final_diagnosis.reason: Lifelong pattern of inattentive symptoms beginning in childhood, with associated restlessness, present across multiple settings and causing clear functional impairment. Symptoms are not progressive and are not better explained by depression, medical illness, or a neurocognitive disorder.
